notes:
Checked 2026-10-09 (America/New_York). Read the entire saved markdown conversion, all 401907 characters, through Appendix BC on PDF p. 216. The saved PDF has 216 pages and zero embedded files. Quotations were checked with PyMuPDF against the indicated PDF pages; only extraction whitespace and zero-width spacing were normalized.

The saved paper contains no explicit data-availability statement, code-release statement, preregistration link, repository identifier, or promise to provide data on request. The p. 29 storage statement says the researchers saved EEG, essays, ChatGPT/browser logs and recordings; it does not say those records are publicly accessible. The form's data_and_code.data_url and code_url are both empty. The corresponding-author email on p. 1 is a general contact, not an on-request data statement; no contact or access request was made.

All study-resource links found in the paper were checked using unauthenticated Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1. https://www.brainonllm.com/ returned HTTP 200; it presents the abstract, limitations and navigation to the preprint, FAQ, figures, videos and reading list. https://www.brainonllm.com/faq, https://www.brainonllm.com/figures, https://www.brainonllm.com/video and https://www.brainonllm.com/reading each returned HTTP 200. No participant-data file, analysis-code repository, data-access terms or preregistration was identified on these pages. The figures page contains 96 image elements and no linked CSV, spreadsheet, archive, participant-data JSON or named data-repository download. The website's GitHub link is the coauthor's profile, not a named repository; no GitHub API requests were made.

The PDF p. 1 license hyperlink, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/, returned HTTP 200 and establishes CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for the paper. The project website also displays this license. No participant-data license was found.

The publisher/preprint landing page https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08872 returned HTTP 200. It identifies v2, revised 31 December 2025, and describes 216 pages, 102 figures, 4 tables and appendix; no supplementary participant-data link is listed. This landing-page information alone does not prove the exact revision identity of the local PDF. https://api.datacite.org/dois/10.48550/arxiv.2506.08872 returned HTTP 200 and identifies the item as a Preprint with relatedIdentifiers=[]. The publication and project website are recorded here as checked locations, rather than counted as data deposits.

Public material within the paper consists of task prompts (pp. 25-27), interview questions (p. 30), model-prompt/architecture figures (pp. 56, 65, 68, 72), outcome plots and the appendix. Appendix A contains interview-cluster descriptions without participant-level records; Appendix B illustrates EEG for participants 36 and 43; the remaining appendices report EEG connectivity summaries, electrode-pair results and session comparisons. They do not provide participant-linked essay scores, complete essays, arm/session identifiers or analysis code needed for the Atlas outcomes. Printed figures, illustrative excerpts and published aggregate tables are not treated as a separate public-data deposit.

The closest Dataset-tagged search result, https://zenodo.org/api/records/19965129 (HTTP 200), is Minsu Cho's Self-Knowledge as Condition Zero for Effective AI Use. Its description cites Kosmyna but describes a separate framework. The API lists one file, 42.SVRN_OS_L3_Before the Prompt Self-Knowledge as Condition Zero for Effective AI Use.pdf (514521 bytes), access_right=open and license cc-by-4.0. It is excluded because it is not a deposit for c416. The OSF theoretical-project false positive is documented with its API file inventory in searches. No relevant participant-level or output-level data file was found to download or inspect.

No missing statistic in final.open_items can currently be computed from confirmed public participant data. In particular, participant-linked teacher/AI scores, per-person and arm means/SDs/SEs, analyzed counts by outcome/session, matched session-4 contrasts, writer-restricted semantic diversity, NER contingency statistics and n-gram specifications remain unavailable. No inference of on-request or restricted access is made from the absence of a deposit. Confidence is high for the documented sources checked; unindexed or subsequently released deposits cannot be ruled out.
